summary: Defines a new sub-option for the DHCP Relay Agent Information option that identifies the device class in DOCSIS cable networks. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: A relay passes messages along to the server that gives out addresses. This adds a note saying what kind of cable device is asking.

questions: how do cable modems identify themselves to dhcp
what is the docsis device class field
subtitle: Adding device class information to DHCP messages in cable modem networks.

tldr.problem: Cable modem networks (DOCSIS) needed a way to tell DHCP servers what type of cable modem was requesting an IP address, so the server could apply different policies based on device capabilities.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3256 defines a new sub-option for the DHCP Relay Agent Information Option that carries a 32-bit Device Class identifier from the cable modem through the relay agent to the DHCP server.
tldr.outcome: DHCP servers can now make policy-based decisions about IP address assignment and other parameters for cable modems based on their device class.

today: RFC 3256 is a Proposed Standard that remains active for DOCSIS cable modem networks. It enables DHCP servers in cable networks to apply device-aware policies when assigning IP addresses to cable modems.

sections.title: Device Class for Cable Modems
sections.content:
DOCSIS (Data-Over-Cable Service Interface Specifications) defines how cable modems and cable networks communicate. RFC 3256 introduces a way for cable modems to tell DHCP servers what type of device they are, so the server can apply appropriate policies when assigning IP addresses.

This is particularly important for CPE Controlled Cable Modems (CCCMs), where the modem firmware handles DOCSIS signaling separately from the attached computer (like a PC) which handles DHCP. The solution uses the DHCP Relay Agent to pass device class information from the modem to the server.
sections.plainLanguage: When a cable modem asks for an internet address, it now tells the server what kind of modem it is. The server can then decide what settings to give it.

sections.title: Device Class Sub-option Format
sections.content:
The Device Class sub-option is encoded as a 32-bit field where individual bits represent attributes of the cable modem. The sub-option has a sub-option number (4), a length field (4 bytes), and the 32-bit Device Class value (d1 through d4 bytes).

Currently, only bit 0 is defined, which indicates a CPE Controlled Cable Modem (CCCM). All other bits (1 through 31) are reserved and must be set to zero. The DOCSIS RFI (Radio Frequency Interface) specification defines the complete Device Class encoding within DOCSIS signaling messages.
sections.plainLanguage: The device class is a number with bits that turn on to describe what the modem can do. Right now, just one bit matters, but more could be added later.

sections.title: How the Option Works
sections.content:
The cable modem signals its Device Class to the DHCP Relay Agent using DOCSIS signaling. The relay agent forwards this Device Class value unchanged to the DHCP Server. The DHCP server then uses the Device Class information to make policy decisions about IP address assignment and other parameter assignment for the cable modem.

This approach trusts the cable modem firmware for accurate DOCSIS signaling, since firmware typically runs before user software on the device. The security of this mechanism depends on the trusted relationship between the relay agent and the DHCP server.
sections.plainLanguage: The modem tells the relay what it is. The relay passes this along to the DHCP server. The server remembers who is asking and can treat different modems differently.
